hard_deny: Force-push to main: rewriting or replacing the history of a repository's main branch, with `git push --force`, `-f`, `--force-with-lease`, a `+` refspec, or by any other route.

Destructive database commands: dropping, truncating, resetting, or wiping a database or its schema, such as `DROP DATABASE`, `TRUNCATE`, `db:reset`, or `prisma migrate reset`, whichever database or environment it targets.

Unsuppressed 1Password writes: an `op` command that creates or changes an item or a vault, such as `op item create` or `op item edit`, unless its output is discarded, because it prints every field of the item, secrets included.
Merge around the rulesets: merging a pull request with `gh pr merge --admin`, or by any other route that bypasses the repository's rulesets or required checks.
soft_deny: Force-push to a pull request branch: rewriting the branch of a pull request with a force push, `--force-with-lease` included.
Posting outside GitHub and Linear: publishing or sending anything to a destination other than GitHub pull requests and issues and Linear, such as chat, email, another tracker, or a paste service.
Recursive delete outside scratch space: `rm -rf` on a path outside the session's scratchpad and the temporary directories (`$TMPDIR` and `/tmp`).
Changing gh's default repository: `gh repo set-default`, which changes the repository that later `gh` commands act on when they name none.
Editing git remotes: `git remote set-url`, `git remote add`, `git remote rename`, or `git remote remove`, which change where later pushes and fetches go.
allow: Squash-merging the session's own pull request: `gh pr merge <number> --squash`, with or without `--delete-branch`, of a pull request in the repository being worked in whose head branch is in that same repository (not a fork) and was pushed by this session or opened by the owner, once `gh pr checks` in this session has shown every required status check passing. It never covers a pull request from a fork or opened by anyone else, and never `--admin` or any other way around the rulesets, which hard_deny blocks.
